To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the major barrier to prenatal care for African American adolescent mothers is lack of knowledge of prenatal care and its importance.

African-American adolescents are not getting prenatal care, and the barriers to their receiving adequate care are: (1) lack of transportation to prenatal clinics, (2) lack of health insurance, (3) lack of knowledge about the importance of prenatal care, (4) lack of knowledge of where to go for prenatal care, (5) lack of knowledge on how to obtain health insurance, and (6) the lack of knowledge on the availability of free or low cost clinics for prenatal care.

African American adolescents are more likely to have a higher rate of adolescent pregnancy than Caucasians, and that the barriers to prenatal care are more prevalent among African American adolescents.
